judged_text: LarkCalendarService.createEvent (and createAttendees at line 163) ignores the credentialId argument and always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId as the calendarId, so every host's credential targets the first host's Lark calendar. For a collective booking with multiple Lark hosts, each secondary host's createEvent runs with their own token against the first host's calendarId and fails, so those hosts' calendars never receive the event — the multi-host fix only works on Google.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Calendar.createEvent` to require `(event, credentialId)` (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts) and `CalendarManager.createEvent` now always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts). However, `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (and its `createAttendees`) still derive `calendarId` from the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) and do not use any `credentialId` to pick the matching destination calendar. Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` to create events per destination/credential (packages/core/EventManager.ts), but it passes the same `event` object (containing the full destinationCalendar array) into each create call. Therefore, for non-Google calendars like Lark, each host/credential will target `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, which can cause secondary hosts to try inserting into the first host's calendar with their own token, matching the reported failure mode.
